system_overview: This specification models the Two-Phase Commit protocol, in which a transaction manager (TM) coordinates a set of resource managers (RMs) to reach agreement on whether to commit or abort a distributed transaction. The protocol implements the abstract transaction commit specification by adding an explicit coordinator and message-passing communication. Only safety properties are specified; liveness (progress) is not modeled.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a transaction manager and a finite set of resource managers that communicate by message passing. The transaction manager collects preparation votes from RMs, makes a global commit-or-abort decision, and broadcasts the result. Resource managers independently prepare (vote to commit) or choose to abort, and act on the transaction manager's decision when it arrives.
state_variables: The system tracks four pieces of state: (1) A mapping from each resource manager to its current state (working, prepared, committed, or aborted). (2) The transaction manager's state (initial, committed, or aborted). (3) The set of resource managers from which the transaction manager has received preparation messages. (4) The set of all messages that have ever been sent, which grows monotonically and is never reduced. Messages are of three types: a preparation message identifying a specific resource manager, a commit broadcast, or an abort broadcast.
initial_state: All resource managers are in the working state. The transaction manager is in its initial state. No resource managers have been recorded as prepared by the transaction manager. No messages have been sent.
actions: The transaction manager has three actions: (1) Receive prepared: while in its initial state, record that a specific RM has sent a preparation message. (2) Commit: if the TM is in its initial state and has received preparation messages from every RM, transition to committed and broadcast a commit message. (3) Abort: if the TM is in its initial state, transition to aborted and broadcast an abort message. Each resource manager has four actions: (1) Prepare: a working RM transitions to prepared and sends a preparation message to the TM. (2) Choose to abort: a working RM spontaneously transitions to aborted without sending any message. (3) Receive commit: upon seeing a commit broadcast, an RM transitions to committed. (4) Receive abort: upon seeing an abort broadcast, an RM transitions to aborted.
safety_properties: Type correctness: all state variables remain within their declared types at all times. The protocol implements the abstract transaction commit specification, meaning the consistency invariant holds: no resource manager is aborted while another is committed.
model_bounds: The set of resource managers is a constant. For model checking, it is typically instantiated with three resource managers.
additional_assumptions: Messages are modeled as a set that only grows; messages are never removed or lost. An action that in a real implementation would be triggered by receiving a message is here enabled by the existence of that message in the sent set. This simplification is valid because only safety properties are specified: there is no requirement that messages be received, so message loss and non-receipt are indistinguishable. The specification imports the abstract transaction commit module and asserts refinement: the two-phase commit protocol implements the abstract specification. Abort messages from RMs to the TM are omitted for simplicity; the TM's spontaneous abort action represents this.
